$comment: HOW THIS FILE WORKS
This is a fitlog program file. The app ships with this copy as a built-in
demo; the same format is used for personal program files imported into the
app (the 'Load program' button, or sharing the file to the installed app on
Android). An imported file replaces the whole program list at once. Weights
entered during workouts are stored separately on the device — never here.
Top level:
weightStep - number > 0: kilograms added/removed by one tap of the -/+
buttons on a weight.
programs   - non-empty array of programs, one per training day; the
picker screen lists them in this order. Ids must be unique.
Program fields:
id        - string, stable key. Weight history is stored under the pair
(program id, exercise id), so renaming an id detaches the
history attached to it. Never reuse or rename ids.
name      - string, the card title on the picker, e.g. 'Workout A'.
day       - string shown above the name, e.g. 'Tuesday'. Display only.
exercises - non-empty array, shown in this order. Ids unique within the
program.
Exercise fields:
id            - string, stable key; same rule as the program id.
name          - string shown on the exercise card.
sets          - optional positive integer. Omit it for warm-ups and
similar unstructured work; when present the card shows
'sets×reps' and the weight can be split per set.
reps          - string, display only. Free form: '10-12', '8 per side',
'20-30 sec per side', '5 min'.
tracksWeight  - optional boolean, default true. Set false for bodyweight
or timed work: the card then shows no weight controls.
initialWeight - optional number, kg to prefill before any history exists.
note          - optional string, a one-line technique cue shown under the
exercise name and highlighted on the guide screen.
guide         - optional object; when present the exercise thumbnail
opens a technique screen (marked with '?').
Guide fields:
steps  - non-empty array of strings, one instruction per list item.
images - optional array of photos, usually two: start and end position.
In this bundled demo they are paths relative to public/, e.g.
'exercises/leg-press-0.jpg'. In an imported file every image
must be self-contained: a data URL of the form
'data:image/jpeg;base64,<base64-encoded bytes>' (jpeg, png and
webp all work). scripts/pack-program.mjs converts file paths to
data URLs, but the file can just as well be written directly in
that form without any script.
Every imported file is validated against the rules above; a file that
breaks them is refused with the reason shown on the button. Unknown fields,
including this $comment, are ignored and dropped on import.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.note: Short range: stop before the pelvis tucks

steps: Feet shoulder width on the middle of the platform, back and hips flat against the seat.
Lower only as far as the pelvis stays pinned to the seat. The moment the tailbone starts to curl up, the range is over.
Press through the heels and stop short of locking the knees.
Prefer more weight over more depth: depth is what loads the spine here, not the weight.
Set the seat height so the handles line up with the middle of the chest.
Back and head stay against the pad for the whole set.
Press until the elbows are almost straight, then return under control.
Do not let the shoulders roll forward at the end of the press.
Grip slightly wider than the shoulders, thighs locked under the pads.
Lean back a few degrees and hold that angle — the torso does not rock.
Pull the bar to the upper chest by driving the elbows down and back.
Let the bar rise under control without the shoulders yanking at the top.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge (dumbbell)
exercises.note: Stop at a straight line, do not arch the lower back

steps: Shoulder blades on the bench or the floor, feet flat, heels under the knees.
Hold the dumbbell across the hip crease with both hands.
Drive through the heels until torso and thighs form a straight line.
Stop there: any extra height comes from arching the lower back, not from the glutes.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control instead of dropping.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.note: Hold 5-8 sec, keep the hips level

steps: Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, spine neutral.
Extend the opposite arm and leg only to shoulder and hip height.
Keep the hips level — the raised side must not rotate upward.
Hold 5-8 seconds, return under control, then switch sides.
Pad just above the heels, hips flat against the bench.
Curl until the heels come close to the glutes without the hips lifting.
Lower slowly — the negative is the point of this one.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.note: Pull with the shoulder blades, torso still

steps: Knees slightly bent, chest up, torso vertical and still.
Start the pull by drawing the shoulder blades together, then bend the elbows.
Bring the handle to the lower ribs with the elbows close to the body.
Return without letting the torso get dragged forward.
Back flat against the vertical pad, feet planted on the floor.
Start with the dumbbells at ear height, elbows slightly in front of the body.
Press up without a hard lockout and without letting the ribs flare.
Lower under control back to ear height.
Knee joint aligned with the machine's pivot, pad resting on the lower shin.
Extend smoothly and pause for a beat at the top.
Lower under control; do not swing the weight up.
Elbow directly under the shoulder, knees bent behind you.
Lift the hips until shoulder, hip and knee form a straight line.
Keep the hips stacked — the top hip does not rotate forward or back.
Breathe normally, hold 20-30 seconds, then switch sides.
Photos show the full version on the feet; you do the same shape from the knees.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
exercises.note: One dumbbell, do not lean sideways

steps: One dumbbell in one hand, arm hanging, shoulders level.
Stand tall and brace the trunk before the first step.
Walk 30 m without leaning toward or away from the weight.
Switch hands and repeat, then set the weight down under control.
